---
title: "Install"
subtitle: "Choose a version before you choose an installation method."
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Try it on a disposable project
Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds
(`proj build`) can modify or remove files, and safety fixes are still pending.
**Never run production builds on the only copy of important work.**
Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Release transition
The published v0.3.0 package predates the recent development changes.
The repaired release and installer routes are still being verified.
A current binary-download route is not yet recommended. The source-build route
below has been checked in Ubuntu CI and requires Rust.
:::

## Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu

Run Linux commands **inside Ubuntu**, including when Ubuntu runs through WSL.
For the first analysis example you need:

- The current preview build of projcli, with its source revision recorded.
- Python 3, including a `python3` command.
- A terminal and a writable folder for the example.

Check Python:

```bash
python3 --version
```

The [published v0.3.0 release](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.3.0)
has an `amd64.deb` asset for Debian-style systems on x86-64 processors.
It is a historical package, not the current preview used by this tutorial.
No current-preview download command is listed here until the replacement
release has been checked.

## Building from source

This route needs Git, a current stable Rust toolchain with Cargo, and your
platform's C/C++ linker tools. The crate uses Rust's 2024 edition.
Ubuntu commonly supplies the linker tools through `build-essential`.

The source-install command below was [verified on Ubuntu in CI](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39489440429)
on 20 October 2026. That run installed
[source revision `fafce46a`](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/commit/fafce46aaba458ef0fbef65718a81076c0a46b40)
and ran both documented examples through the CLI:

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli --locked --bin proj
```

This command installs the current repository source, which can change after
that check. It does not install the historical release package.

Cargo normally places the command in `~/.cargo/bin`; that folder must be on
your `PATH`. Record the installed commit from Cargo's output when trying a
development build. The version number alone does not identify the recent
features.

## Check which command you have

Another program can also use the name `proj`. In Ubuntu, check both its
location and its help:

```bash
command -v proj
proj --help
```

For this project's current preview, help lists `build-dev`, `--project`
and `--non-interactive`. If those are missing, check which executable your
shell found before continuing.

## Other systems

Windows amd64 builds are exercised in CI. A released native Windows installer
has not yet been verified for the current preview. Published macOS and ARM
binary assets have not been established either. Rust test coverage on a
platform does not establish that a release installer works there.

## Extra tools depend on your project

The [first tutorial](tutorial.qmd) uses only Python's standard library.
R scripts need R and `Rscript`; reports may additionally need Quarto,
`rmarkdown` or `bookdown`. Install the tools required by your own targets
before running them. Git and remote credentials are needed only for workflows
that use those integrations.
